pattern.crimePattern: a security contractor paid from the Mvua till kills the defence advocate who was about to talk to the prosecutor, and frames the prosecutor with her own pen and paper
pattern.notes: Fictional tower, firm, contractor and ODPP clerk. Region 9 boss. Halima is the framed suspect and tells the truth from the first interview. The SIM that lured her uses the same dead man's ID as the phone in case 50. After the verdict the envelope narrows Kivuli to three names (provisional, pending the cultural reader).

ob.text: Advocate Sharon Kiprop (46) is found dead in her chambers on the ninth floor of Jacaranda Towers, Westlands. On Tuesday morning DCI officers arrest Prosecutor Halima Abdi. At noon the Officer Commanding gives Amani the case: "You know her. That's why it's you, and that's why you'll do it by the book."

facts.text: Advocate Sharon Kiprop was found dead in her ninth-floor chambers on Monday morning; on Tuesday the DCI arrested Prosecutor Halima Abdi.
One blow to Sharon's head; a marble bookend on the carpet, wiped. Her laptop is missing.
The document safe is untouched but scratched around the dial.
Under the desk: a black fountain pen engraved "H. Abdi — from Baba".
On the desk, typed: "Withdraw the complaint against me or you will regret it. — H.A."
The DCI file: the pen, the note, the sign-in entry "H. Abdi — 21:45", Sharon's misconduct complaint against Halima, and Halima's reply to "S.K.": "I'll be there at 9."
Sign-in book: Halima's entry reads "21:45", written over an erased "21:00" in a different pen.
Under raking light, against the lobby camera: the entry was first "21:00", the minute Halima walked in; it was changed later.
Lobby camera: Halima in at 21:00, out at 21:14. Sharon in at 21:32. No one else through the lobby until 23:00.
Halima left the tower at 21:14 and never came back: the lobby camera, and the service lift needs a master card.
Patrick was at the lobby desk on camera all night.
Halima: "Someone signing as S.K. texted at ten past eight. I went at nine. The guard said she wasn't in but I could go up. I knocked, waited, left. My pen went missing on Friday; I reported it."
ODPP log: "Friday 17:30 — H. Abdi — fountain pen, black, engraved — missing from desk." Cynthia Moraa, the records clerk, was alone in the section that afternoon.
Halima's ten-print card from her ODPP staff file.
Faith: on Friday Sharon said her safe's white envelope goes to Prosecutor Abdi if anything happens to her, and gave Faith the combination, sealed. Her partner and Lydia Emojong quarrelled with her.
Faith was at home on a video call with her mother 21:30–22:30.
In Sharon's safe: a white envelope addressed "Prosecutor H. Abdi — only".
Records ①: the S.K. SIM is registered to the ID of a man dead ten years, the same ID as the phone that called Walter Ogada. Used once: the 20:10 text, from the Kasarani mast.
Records ②: at 21:05 Mwita's phone called Sharon for one minute.
Records ②: the Mlinzi Bora master card took the service lift up to the ninth floor at 21:35, into the corridor beside Sharon's office, and down at 22:16; car park exit 22:20.

Records ②: on Monday Mlinzi Bora received KSh 2,000,000 from Till 880 214, "security consultancy".
Records ②: Cynthia's own line was on the Kasarani mast all Sunday evening.
Cynthia hands over the S.K. SIM from her phone-case pocket and a printout of Halima's diary page for the week.
In the Major's safe: Sharon's laptop.
In the Major's safe: a pair of shoe covers in a bin bag, stained.
Kenneth was at a golf tournament in Nanyuki from Friday to Monday.
Her church and her sister: Lydia was at an all-night prayer vigil in Buruburu on Sunday.
Fingerprints taken from Major Mwita in detention.
Post-mortem: one blow from a heavy, smooth-edged object, matching the bookend.
Post-mortem: death on Sunday between 21:40 and 22:15.
Lab: Halima's prints are under the toner: the ridges show beneath the printed letters. Nothing on top of the toner at all.

Lab: the stains on the shoe covers are Sharon's blood.

reconstruction.text: After Emojong's arrest, Sharon understands that Kivuli's people will decide she knows too much. On Thursday she emails Halima from a private address asking to meet "about my clients' instructing party".

On Friday Cynthia, paid by Mlinzi Bora for a year, reads the email on Halima's screen and tells Major Mwita. That afternoon she takes Halima's engraved pen and three blank sheets from the printer tray Halima loaded that morning.

Sunday, 20:10. Cynthia sends the "S.K." text from a dead man's SIM. Halima comes at nine, knocks on a locked door and leaves at 21:14. At 21:05 Mwita calls Sharon in about an "alarm"; she arrives at 21:32.

At 21:35 Mwita rides the camera-less service lift up on his master card. He strikes Sharon with a marble bookend, fails at the safe, takes her laptop, and leaves Halima's pen and a note printed on her paper.
He leaves by the car park at 22:20. On Monday morning he has Patrick change Halima's time to 21:45, and Mlinzi Bora receives KSh 2 million from Till 880 214.

afterVerdict.beat: Halima is released on Wednesday evening. She walks into the SCU office without knocking, puts a box of mandazi on Amani's desk and sits down. Then she takes the fountain pen from the evidence bag Rukia signed over and puts it in Amani's hand: "My father gave it to me when I passed the bar. You use it. Sign Kivuli's charge sheet with it."
The white envelope is opened in Halima's presence.
beats: A copy of Sharon's retainer ledger: every client she represented for "M.H." over six years, each instruction marked "per K."

A handwritten page: "Instructions come from a person the others call K. I have never met K knowingly. Instructions reach me through three people, always in person, at a private members' club in Muthaiga: Raphael Oduya, Margaret Kabiru, Stanley Rotich."
"Each of them has at some point said 'K. wants'. Each of them sat on the fourth floor of Lands House twelve years ago. I believe one of them is K. I have never been able to tell which. — S.K."
A photograph: the same one that hangs in Dr. Mwamburi's boardroom (case 86), the fourth-floor launch twelve years ago, with three faces circled in red pen.

files.text: Narrowed to three: Raphael Oduya (then Director of Land Adjudication), Margaret Kabiru (then Deputy Chief Land Registrar, Records), Stanley Rotich (then Chief Valuer). "One of them is K."
The dead man's ID: the same registration behind the phone in case 50 and the lure SIM in case 90.
KSh 2,000,000 from Till 880 214 to Mlinzi Bora the morning after; Sharon's retainer ledger, "per K."

afterVerdict.beat: That night Mwalimu calls. The player reads the three names to her from the notebook (shown as text; Amani is never voiced). A long silence. Then: "I sat across a table from all three at that launch. One of them shook your father's hand that day. I don't know which one sent the order. But I know the fourth floor's corridor by heart, and I'll draw it for you." The next morning a hand-drawn floor plan arrives by courier, three offices marked.

files.text: Mwalimu: one of the three shook Joseph's hand at the launch. Her drawing of the fourth-floor corridor, three offices marked.

afterVerdict.beat: Collectible: Halima's fountain pen, engraved "H. Abdi — from Baba", on Amani's desk from now on.
Amani's notebook, the region's last line: "Oduya. Kabiru. Rotich. One of them is the desk."

clockPlan.note: Three stamps, the maximum: records on the lure SIM, records on Mlinzi Bora (calls, access card, payments), and a warrant on the Major's office. Cynthia hands over the SIM when pressed. The fingerprint layering (6 h) and the sign-in document exam (10 h) go first; detain Mwita after the warrant, and the shoe-cover blood (12 h) comes back inside 24 h.

ui.beatNotes: The framed friend. For the first time, a character the player trusts is on the suspect wall, and Halima's voice is gone from the batch-confirmation feedback: Rukia Hassan's colder lines replace it for this one case. When the charge sheet is accepted, Halima's photo moves off the suspect wall and back to its old place on the desk, beside the phone.
